description:
More than 60 artifacts spanning nearly 10,000 years from one of the most significant sites in Virginia Indian history are on display for the first time in a museum setting. Werowocomoco was the principal residence of Powhatan, paramount chief of 30-some Indian tribes in Virginias coastal region at the time English colonists arrived in 1607. Archaeological excavations have revealed not only that the York River site was a uniquely important place during Powhatans time, but also that its role as a political and social center predated the Powhatan chiefdom. Werowocomoco is the place where Captain John Smith was taken prisoner by Powhatan in 1607 and first met Powhatans daughter Pocahontas.
A detail (at right) from John Smith's Map of Virginia, 1612, shows Powhatan at Werowocomoco. Jamestown-Yorktown Foundation collection.
name: "Werowocomoco:  Seat of Power" Special Exhibition at Jamestown Settlement

description:
The Carter Family Fold welcomes you every Saturday night, carrying on the musical and performing traditions of A.P. Carter, his wife, Sara, and her sister Maybelle at the dawn of the age of country music - an age they helped establish beginning in 1927. And they did it right here where the Carter Fold is today, in Poor Valley, at the foot of the Clinch Mountain in Southwest Virginia.
A Saturday with us in rural southwest Virginia will supply you with an evening of musical entertainment and country hospitality you won't soon forget. Chances are you'll make some new friends and take with you some fond memories. We'd love to have you visit us.
Check our show schedule on our website for performers and more information.
name: Carter Family Fold Weekly Music

description:
Sorrel's will feature the dynamic vocals/guitar duo of Jennifer Kirkland and Bert Carlson every Tuesday night from 6:30-8:30.

They do it all, from creating fresh arrangements of jazz standards, to reinventing pop/rock tunes with their unique style, to presenting their own original material. At the luxurious Stonewall Jackson Hotel, Sorrel's offers a casual dining experience where you can enjoy your favorite beverage or one of our chef's specials.

description:
"Soup-on-Sunday"
Every Sunday fly-in or drive-in to Campbell Field Airport and enjoy soup, hot dogs and other assorted goodies. This is not a fancy fly-in just a good old fashioned "roll on the grass". While you may think the purpose is to feed hungry pilots the real idea is to get those plane engines running. So get that oil warmed up and fly on in! This event is open to all pilots and the non flying public. Meet interesting pilots from all over the east coast, see some amazing aircraft and enjoy the country setting.
The event is canceled if there is inclement weather so always check www.CampbellFieldAirport.com before departing for event status, or call the airport at (757) 442-7519.
name: Soup-on-Sunday at Campbell Field Airport (9VG), Eastern Shore

description:
The Pickin Porch at the Bristol Mall just off exit 1 of I-81 is a weekly showcase of local, regional and national performers. If you like bluegrass, old time, Celtic and Americana music you'll love the Pickin Porch concerts every Thursday evening!
Admission is free but donations are requested thru the non-profit ACMA and proceeds go to benefit the Mountain Music Museum also located in the Bristol Mall which is open 7 days a week and tells the history of the music born in the southern Appalachians.
Young musicians often perform on the Pickin Porch which serves as a venue to help them get a start in the music business. Many experienced regional and national acts also perform. The Pickin Porch is always fun and exciting and is a place to take your entire family!
name: Pickin Porch

description: The Gospel Chicken House celebrates 36 years of continuous Saturday night Gospel Sings in 2009. We invite everyone to join us each and every Saturday night at 6:00 p.m. (except the Saturday between Christmas and New Years). There is never an admission charge. We have new handicap facilities and welcome groups to join us each week. Please call the Chicken House at 804-883-6487 for advance seating of groups of 10 or more. The Chicken House is famous for having some of the best Southern and Bluegrass Gospel Groups perform. A large variety of foods are available at very reasonable prices. All proceeds from the concession sales helps keep the Chicken House operating. A love offering each week to help office the groups with their travel expenses.
name: Gospel Chicken House

description:
The Floyd Country Store, home of the Friday Night Jamboree, was constructed around 1910, and has been an important part of the community ever since. What is still most striking in the store though, is that as people walk through the door they cant help but smile.
The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.
Admission is only $5. Major venue on The Crooked Road.
name: Floyd Country Store Friday Night Jamboree

description: Planning a beach wedding? You may want to participate in some of our "Sunday Beach Wedding Tours" which begin November 14, 2010 and continue every Sunday at 1 pm through March 6, 2011. This is a 2-hour guided tour of the best wedding sites in Virginia Beach - a "traveling consultation" . Which sites are good for sunset pictures? How about sunrise? Which beaches offer a little more privacy? You will find the answers to these questions and more as you preview the different beaches. You will visit several wedding sites and gain valuable advice and tips to help you plan your beach wedding. A little knowledge can help you prevent costly mistakes. Transportation is provided. Reserve the tour online with a $10 reservation fee.

description:
Want to get up close and personal with one of America's most endangered mammals? Imagine finding yourself face to face and 15 feet from the endangered Red Wolf? An Animal Confidential Tour with VLM Curatorial Director George Mathews, Jr. will take you closer than your average visitor.
* Tour the otter and red wolf buildings
* Get closer to the raccoon enclosure and areas along the Outdoor Trail
* Find out the personal stories of our animals and why they are with us as well as what their lives were like before they came to the museum
* Find out what they eat, what activities we do to keep them healthy and observe special enrichment activities with the otter and raccoons
* Each animal species plays a role in the wild. This tour explains the cycle and how these animals are our special ambassadors for their species.
Ages 4+.
name: Animal Confidential at the Virginia Living Museum

description:
Ever wonder what goes on "Behind-the-Scenes" at the Virginia Living Museum? Now is your chance to find out! Guided by a member of our knowledgeable curatorial staff...journey to areas of the museum where daily visitors are not allowed.
* Animal support areas
* Animal food prep facilities
* Aquarium holding facility
* Reptile support unit
* Salt water mixing area
* Climb to the catwalk above the Chesapeake Bay Aquarium...for a scene few have seen!
Join a small group of visitors for a truly unique experience as you learn about how the museum operates from the inside out! Take part in a fish feeding at one of our many habitats. Have your individual questions answered by the experts in a behind-the- scenes tour catered to your interests. Ages 4+, no strollers. Max 10 people.
Tues. and Sat. at 3 p.m.

description:
More than 60 artifacts spanning nearly 10,000 years from one of the most significant sites in Virginia Indian history are on display for the first time in a museum setting. Werowocomoco was the principal residence of Powhatan, paramount chief of 30-some Indian tribes in Virginias coastal region at the time English colonists arrived in 1607. Archaeological excavations have revealed not only that the York River site was a uniquely important place during Powhatans time, but also that its role as a political and social center predated the Powhatan chiefdom. Werowocomoco is the place where Captain John Smith was taken prisoner by Powhatan in 1607 and first met Powhatans daughter Pocahontas.
A detail (at right) from John Smith's Map of Virginia, 1612, shows Powhatan at Werowocomoco. Jamestown-Yorktown Foundation collection.
name: "Werowocomoco:  Seat of Power" Special Exhibition at Jamestown Settlement
